Usage

Projects each point onto a local polynomial surface to remove noise (Moving Least Squares smoothing).

For each point, gathers the neighbours within radius radius, estimates the local plane (normal n and the 2 axes of the tangent plane) by weighted PCA, and fits a polynomial surface of degree order to the neighbours' "tangent-plane coordinates (u,v) → height h along the normal" by Gaussian-weighted least squares. The point of interest itself sits at the origin (0,0) of the local coordinates, so it is moved along the normal by the height of the fitted surface at (0,0) (= the constant term) and thereby projected onto the surface. Only sensor noise is smoothed while the shape of the surface is kept.

Parameters

points : array_like, shape (N, 3)

Input point cloud.

radius : float

Radius of the neighbourhood sphere (> 0). The support of the local surface.

order : int

Degree of the local polynomial (default 2). The number of terms is (order+1)(order+2)/2.

Returns

ndarray, shape (N, 3)

Smoothed point cloud (order and number of points kept). Points whose neighbours are fewer than the polynomial's number of terms stay in place.

Notes

This is an approximation method. Points with fewer neighbours than terms / with a degenerate local plane are not moved and keep their original position (a safety measure so that it does not run wild at holes or borders). radius <= 0 raises ValueError; empty input returns empty.

The 3d op mls_smooth bridged into the 2-D evolution registry. The implementation is the same; only the calling convention is adapted to op(v, a, b). a sweeps order (default 2). b is unused.
